records.author_body: I'm building GazeRank, a website audit tool for SEO, performance, accessibility, and AI search readiness. I'm a solo founder. The app has been online since August, but I only started sharing it publicly on October 1. The numbers so far • 12 signups in the database (4 are my own test accounts) • 3 users ran a scan • 0 came back on a different day • ~30 tracked visits since October 1, probably an undercount Five of the eight non-test signups never ran a scan. Traffic is still tiny, so I can't blame everything on activation. But activation is something I can work on this week. What I've tried • X: A pinned post and a thread sharing data from 285 website scans. A handful of comments. • LinkedIn: 292 impressions, 7 clicks, 0 reactions, and 2 comments on the company page. • Directories: Submitted to 8, including SaaSHub, AlternativeTo, and BetaList. • Product Hunt: Preparing for launch. The directories haven't had enough time to tell me much yet. One interesting finding I scanned 285 websites, mostly SaaS, developer-tool, and marketing sites. • 54% had no content freshness signal. • 52% had low readability. • 51% were missing at least one security header. These findings suggest the issues are common. They don't tell me whether people care enough to scan their own sites, let alone pay to fix them. Full methodology and data: https://www.gazerank.com/reports/benchmark One lesson from building the product Scanning my own site once showed a Performance score of 100 next to a poor Largest Contentful Paint (LCP). I fixed it and wrote about the experience. It reminded me that an audit tool needs to earn trust through evidence, not just scores. What I'm trying this week Email the five people who signed up but never scanned and ask what stopped them. Post from my personal LinkedIn profile instead of only the company page. Reply to every relevant comment with something useful, offering a scan where it makes sense. I'll share what I learn, including if none of it works. Two questions for founders who've been here What got your early signups to actually use your product? Was it a change to onboarding, a personal email, a demo, or something else? What was the first channel that brought you a user who returned the following week? What did you actually do that week? Concrete examples would help more than general advice. And if you'd like a GazeRank scan, drop your URL. I'll run it and share up to three useful findings where possible.

metadata.headline: 8 signups, 3 people scanned, 0 came back. How did you get your first users to stick?
